settings.title: {channel} settings
settings.label: Channel settings
settings.readOnly: Read-only: changing these needs operator status ({prefix}) in {channel}.
settings.canChangeEverything: You’re {rank} here and can change everything below.
settings.canManageLists: As a half-operator you can manage lists and the topic, but not modes.

modes.serverDescription: This network defines what this mode does.
modes.varies: Its exact meaning depends on the server.
modes.registrationHint: Registration, founders and access lists are on the Registration tab.

n.label: No outside messages
n.description: Only people in the channel can send to it.

t.label: Topic lock
t.description: Only operators can change the topic.

m.label: Moderated
m.description: Only voiced people and operators can talk.

i.label: Invite only
i.description: People need an invite (or an invite exception) to join.

s.label: Secret
s.description: Hidden from the channel list and WHOIS.

p.label: Private
p.description: Hidden from WHOIS; listed without its topic.

l.label: User limit
l.description: Nobody else can join once this many people are in.

r.label: Registered only
r.description: Only people logged in to services can join.

R.label: Registered only
R.description: Only people logged in to services can join.

c.label: No colours
c.description: Colour codes are blocked or stripped.

C.label: No CTCP
C.description: CTCP messages (other than ACTION) are blocked.

S.label: TLS only / strip colours
S.description: Only TLS connections may join, or colours are stripped, depending on the server.

T.label: No notices
T.description: Notices to the channel are blocked.

z.label: Reduced moderation
z.description: Blocked messages are shown to operators instead of dropped.

g.label: Free invite
g.description: Anyone in the channel can invite others.

P.label: Permanent
P.description: The channel stays when everyone leaves.

Q.label: No forwarding
Q.description: Users can’t be forwarded into this channel.

F.label: Free forward target
F.description: Anyone can forward users to this channel.

u.label: Unfiltered
u.description: Operators see messages the server would otherwise filter.

f.label: Forward
f.description: Where people go when they can’t join, or a flood limit, depending on the server.

j.label: Join throttle
j.description: Limits how many joins are allowed per interval (joins:seconds).

b.label: Bans
b.description: People matching a ban can’t join.
b.overrides: A ban doesn’t remove anyone already here; kick them too. Ban exceptions override bans.

e.label: Ban exceptions
e.description: People matching an exception can join even when a ban matches them.
e.overrides: It lets them past bans (on some networks, quiets too). Invite-only (+i), the key and the user limit still apply to them.

I.label: Invite exceptions
I.description: People matching an invite exception can join an invite-only channel without an invite.
I.overrides: It overrides invite-only (+i) only: a ban still keeps them out.

q.label: Quiets
q.description: People matching a quiet can’t talk.

broad.host: The host part is very broad: it can match a whole country, provider or address range.
broad.nick: The nick part is very broad: it matches every nick with those few letters.

mask.invalidPrefix: Masks can’t start with “:” or contain commas.
mask.account: Anyone logged in to the account {account}, whatever nick they use.
mask.accountNot: Anyone not logged in to the account {account}, whatever nick they use.
mask.anyAccount: Anyone logged in to an account.
mask.anyAccountNot: Anyone not logged in to an account.
mask.mute: Mutes {parts}: they can stay in the channel but can’t talk.
mask.extended: A server-specific extended mask, sent as typed.
mask.extendedNegated: A server-specific extended mask (negated: it matches everyone the rest doesn’t), sent as typed.
mask.unknownExtban: Sent as typed: this network doesn’t advertise extended masks (EXTBAN), so it may not understand it.
mask.unknownType: This network doesn’t advertise this {prefix} mask type; it’s sent as typed and the server decides.
mask.noExtendedType: This network doesn’t offer {prefix}… extended masks, so it reads this as a nickname.
mask.matchesForward: Matches {parts} and sends them to {channel} instead.
